title: Slab allocator atomic eviction + tenant graceful-degrade to remediate cross-env GPU OOMs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Multiple production escalations across Hosted and Dedicated clusters surfaced a new failure mode: rapid GPU OOM cascades correlated with concurrent KV cache checkpointing and background prefetch on high-concurrency tenants. Symptoms included repeated OOM spikes during nightly steady-state periods, KV integrity errors in logs, and slow memory growth leading to fragmentation and ultimate failure of allocator arenas. Impact: customer-facing sessions failing with 502s, elevated latency, and Dedicated customers experiencing degraded throughput. Root cause hypothesis: a race between the async journal/checkpoint writer and the eviction path caused a tombstone state transition to be observed twice, corrupting slab metadata (double-free / stale pointer) and creating fragmentation plus undetected KV leaks. This manifested as slow memory leak leading to GPU memory exhaustion under bursty workloads. Proposed permanent fix: - Introduce an atomic tombstone state transition (CAS) in the KV index to prevent double-commit races. - Add a per-arena eviction lock (coarse-grained initially) to serialize the critical path between checkpoint/journal and eviction/compaction. - Harden allocator with defensive bounds checks to avoid following stale pointers; add checksum validation for index entries. - Add operational mitigations: emergency tenant-level prefetch throttles, reduce background checkpoint concurrency, increase eviction aggressiveness, and enable per-tenant memory soft-limits with graceful degradation (reject heavy prefetch requests). Testing and rollout: unit tests for CAS transitions, deterministic concurrency tests in the runtime stress rig, and a 48-hour soak on dedicated Canary pool (5% of capacity) before a staged rollout to Hosted. Metrics to monitor: oom_count, kv_index_checksum_errors, slab_fragmentation_ratio, eviction_latency_p50/p95, tenant_prefetch_rate. Rollback plan: if OOMs or latency regressions increase by >20% vs baseline, roll back to previous runtime and enable temporary throttles. Deliverables: PR with runtime patch, updated runbook, telemetry dashboards, changelog entry, and postmortem. Links provided below.

resolution_notes: Patch introduces atomic tombstone state transition and per-arena eviction lock. Canary shows OOM reductions and KV integrity improvement. Performance tradeoff: eviction p95 increased ~6% on canary, within SLA. Plan to optimize lock granularity in follow-up (ENG-784010) to recover latency while preserving safety.
